memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses then took the blood, sprinkled it on the people and said, 'This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.'" - Exodus 24:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The moment arrives. Moses sprinkles the blood on the people and declares, "This is the blood of the covenant." With those words, Israel was marked as God's own. The blood touched them personally — this was not an abstract agreement but something applied directly to the people themselves. They now belonged to Him in a bond sealed with life.

There is something deeply moving about blood being applied, not merely poured out at a distance. It had to touch them. In the same way, Christ's sacrifice is not merely a historical fact to admire from afar; it must be personally received. The gospel is not only that Jesus died, but that He died for you, and that His work is applied to your own heart by faith.

Jesus deliberately echoed these very words at the Last Supper: "This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many" (Mark 14:24). He was announcing that the shadow had met its substance. What Moses did with a bowl of animal blood, Christ accomplished with His own. If you belong to Jesus, you have been marked as God's own — claimed, cleansed, and secured. Whatever else may be uncertain in your life, this is settled: you belong to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have I personally received what Christ accomplished, or do I admire it from a distance?
What does it mean to me today that I belong to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, Your blood was poured out for me personally, not merely for the world in general. Thank You that I belong to God, claimed and cleansed by You. Amen.
